title: Zoom vs Webex
description: Zoom vs Webex: compare meeting limits, paid plans, calling, recordings, administration, integrations, and AI features. Both offer a free plan; the best fit depends on whether your team prioritizes Zoom Workplace's broader workspace or Webex's meeting and calling bundles.

features.name: Free meetings
features.tool1Detail: Zoom Basic is free and lists meetings up to 40 minutes with up to 100 participants. Confirm current limits and regional terms on Zoom's pricing page.
features.tool2Detail: Webex Free is free and lists meetings up to 40 minutes with up to 100 attendees. Availability and some terms depend on country; confirm the current regional offer.

features.name: Paid meeting plan
features.tool1Detail: Zoom Workplace Pro is listed at $16.99 per user/month billed monthly or $14.16 billed annually. It extends meeting duration and adds cloud recording and other workspace features; verify the current plan details.
features.tool2Detail: Webex Meet is listed at $14.50 per user/month billed monthly or $12 billed annually on its current US pricing page. It supports meetings up to 24 hours and up to 200 attendees; confirm country-specific pricing.

features.name: Meeting capacity
features.tool1Detail: Zoom lists up to 100 participants on Basic and Pro, and up to 300 on Business, with add-ons available for larger meetings. Verify the tier required for your event size.
features.tool2Detail: Webex lists up to 100 attendees on Free, up to 200 on Meet, and up to 1,000 on Enterprise. Confirm the plan and any event-specific limits.

features.name: Calling features
features.tool1Detail: Zoom Workplace includes VoIP calling; full-featured business phone capabilities and phone plans depend on the selected subscription or add-on.
features.tool2Detail: Webex Suite Meet + Call combines meetings with a business phone number and calling features. International calling and add-ons may be billed separately.

features.name: Recording and follow-up
features.tool1Detail: Zoom plan details distinguish local recording, cloud storage, and enterprise recording options. Check storage limits, retention, and which AI meeting features are included.
features.tool2Detail: Webex Meet lists 10 GB AI-powered cloud recording; Enterprise lists local and unlimited cloud recording. Verify storage, retention, and AI feature terms for your plan.

features.name: Administration and security
features.tool1Detail: Zoom lists SSO and managed domains on Business, alongside other administration controls. Verify security settings, retention, identity features, and contractual requirements for your deployment.
features.tool2Detail: Webex plans vary in administration and security features, with enterprise offerings adding further controls. Confirm SSO, logging, data residency, and any compliance obligations with the vendor.

features.name: AI meeting features
features.tool1Detail: Zoom plan pages list AI Companion features with usage and capability differences by tier. Test summary quality and review data-handling settings before enabling it for sensitive meetings.
features.tool2Detail: Webex includes AI Assistant on paid meeting plans in its current plan listing. Validate summaries, transcription, language support, retention, and data controls against your needs.

features.name: Integrations and workflow fit
features.tool1Detail: Zoom lists integrations with common workplace systems. Test calendar, identity, CRM, recording, and meeting workflows that your team depends on.
features.tool2Detail: Webex integrates with workplace systems and is part of Cisco's collaboration ecosystem. Test your required calendar, identity, calling, and contact-center integrations.

features.name: Best fit
features.tool1Detail: Consider Zoom when your organization already uses Zoom Workplace or wants meetings alongside chat, mail, calendar, docs, and related workspace features.
features.tool2Detail: Consider Webex when meetings need to connect closely with Webex calling, Cisco collaboration devices, or an existing Cisco communications environment.

verdict:
Quick verdict

Zoom and Webex both provide free meetings and paid options, so the choice should be based on how your organization communicates. Zoom Workplace brings meetings together with chat, mail, calendar, docs, and related work features. Webex offers meeting plans and bundles that can add business calling, with deeper fit for organizations already using Cisco collaboration and calling products.

Pricing checked on October 9, 2026

Zoom lists Basic as free, Pro at $16.99 per user/month billed monthly or $14.16 billed annually, and Business at $21.99 billed monthly or $18.33 billed annually. Webex lists Free at $0, Meet at $14.50 per user/month billed monthly or $12 billed annually, and Suite Meet + Call at $25 billed monthly or $22.50 billed annually. These are vendor-listed US prices; country, taxes, promotions, add-ons, and billing terms can change the final cost. Confirm the current terms on the official Zoom pricing page and official Webex pricing page.

Where Zoom may fit better

Consider Zoom when your organization already uses Zoom Workplace or wants meetings combined with chat, mail, calendar, docs, and related collaboration features. Compare meeting capacity, cloud storage, AI feature limits, identity controls, and phone requirements before deciding which plan to buy.

Where Webex may fit better

Consider Webex when meetings need to connect with Webex calling, Cisco collaboration devices, or an existing Cisco communications environment. The Meet plan lists meetings up to 24 hours and up to 200 attendees; the Meet + Call bundle adds a business phone number and calling features. Confirm country availability and any international calling charges.

Security and regulated workflows

Do not assume that every plan or default configuration meets a regulated workflow's requirements. Verify the exact plan, contract, configuration, retention behavior, access controls, and any required business associate or data-processing agreement directly with the vendor and your compliance owner before handling sensitive information.

Run a practical pilot

Test the meetings your organization actually hosts: internal calls, external guests, larger sessions, recording, captions, calendar scheduling, screen sharing, mobile joining, and any phone-system handoff. Measure call quality on your normal networks, confirm the attendee capacity you need, and test how administrators handle access and retention.

Sources and freshness

Plan details checked on 2026-10-09 using Zoom Workplace pricing and Webex Meetings pricing. Verify current plan limits and prices before purchase.

faqs.question: Is Zoom or Webex cheaper?
faqs.answer: Both have free plans. On the current US pricing pages, Zoom Pro is listed at $16.99 per user/month billed monthly or $14.16 billed annually, while Webex Meet is $14.50 monthly or $12 billed annually. Compare the same billing interval, meeting capacity, storage, calling, and add-ons before deciding.

faqs.question: Do Zoom and Webex free plans have the same meeting limits?
faqs.answer: Both currently list free meetings up to 40 minutes and up to 100 participants or attendees. Confirm current terms and regional availability directly with each vendor before relying on those limits.

faqs.question: Which platform is better for enterprise use?
faqs.answer: Compare the actual enterprise requirements: attendee capacity, calling, identity and admin controls, retention, audit needs, data processing terms, integrations, and support commitments. The better choice depends on your existing collaboration stack and the exact plan.

faqs.question: Can either platform be used for healthcare or other regulated meetings?
faqs.answer: Do not infer compliance from a product name or a feature checklist. Confirm the eligible plan, contract, required agreement, configuration, retention, and permitted data flows directly with the vendor and your compliance owner before handling regulated information.
